elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained opening of 15.3(b): "The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to ..." — the cap runs to both IBM (Customer) and MSL (Vendor).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered text caps at "the fees paid or payable by IBM to MSL under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" with no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor. To reach preferred, insert the alternative USD 1,000,000 limb.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 15.3(a): "Neither Party will be liable to the other for lost profits, consequential, punitive, or incidental damages ..." — mutual by its terms.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "provided that this limitation does not apply to either Party's ... breach of its confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The proviso lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; data protection and security obligations are absent and therefore remain inside the cap.
"this limitation does not apply to either Party's indemnification obligations" — this pulls MSL's Section 15.1 indemnities outside the cap.
"... gross negligence ..." expressly listed in the carve-out proviso.
"... or willful misconduct" expressly listed in the carve-out proviso.
No reference to fraud anywhere in the rendered 15.3; fraud liability remains capped. Add "fraud" to the proviso for preferred.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The proviso does not carve out infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights as a stand-alone head; the indemnification carve-out only reaches liabilities arising under the indemnity obligations, not direct IP infringement claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No sentence states that IBM's obligation to pay amounts due under the Agreement is not "damages" subject to the cap; add an express exclusion for Customer payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "The total liability for either Party ... is limited to ..." — unchanged mutual structure covering IBM and MSL.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Basis changed from 3% of bill-of-materials value over the life of the Agreement to "the fees paid or payable by IBM to MSL under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim".
"provided that this limitation does not apply to either Party's indemnification obligations".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "... breach of its confidentiality obligations" listed in the proviso.
"... gross negligence ..." listed in the proviso.
"... or willful misconduct" listed in the proviso.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: all six fallback elements are met in operative language (mutual cap retained, basis changed to fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim, and a single proviso adding indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct carve-outs).

Preferred is not met: the USD 1,000,000 floor, the data protection/security carve-out, fraud, infringement of the other party's IP, and the Customer-payment-obligations exclusion are all absent. If the drafter wants preferred, amend 15.3(b) to read "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable ... in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000", extend the proviso to data protection and security obligations, fraud and infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights, and add a sentence that IBM's obligation to pay amounts due is not subject to the cap.

Minimality holds: 15.3(a)'s mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the opening mutual wording of 15.3(b) are preserved verbatim; only the illusory 3% bill-of-materials basis was replaced and one carve-out proviso added. No survival tails, expense language, procedures or extra damages categories were introduced, and no favourable existing wording was deleted.

Intent preserved: the change is confined to the cap basis and carve-outs; the tort/contract framing, Section 15.1 indemnities and the separate Equipment and Program Loan Agreement cap (favourable to IBM) are untouched, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling. Note the fee basis is expressly directional ("paid or payable by IBM to MSL"), which keeps the cap workable when MSL is the liable party.

Finding classification of "deviation" is correct: the original clause put MSL's Section 15.1 indemnities (including IP infringement) inside a 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap with no carve-outs, which is walk-away territory under the rule.
